B38.capture_spec: C38-soft-edges: scene spec evidence/planning-checks/scenes/C38-soft-edges.json, 13.3 s clip (stretched to the measured audio), 30 fps, 1280x720 canvas rendered at 3840x2160, Forward+, nearest filter. A 12x look at the rim of the soft-edged sprite: plain mix leaves pale, see-through rim pixels (alpha 0.75 at worst) on both sides; as the voice says 'compute the alpha yourself' the right side switches to the composite, which makes them opaque. Verified: 224 rim pixels all see-through with plain mix (output alpha 0.75 to 0.95, mean 0.82), 0 with the composite (alpha 1.00); on hard-edged art the two give the same picture (analyze_soft B1; analyze_lab A13); in the capture 7,056 canvas px of the right panel change at the switch and none of the left (analyze_scenes C38)
B38.visual_intent: Code card at left: the 14-line composite shader (edge, alpha and the vec4 line marked). At right two real 12x close-ups of the rim of a soft-edged sprite, both on the plain mix: pale, see-through pixels sit between the teal and the line. As the voice says 'compute the alpha yourself' the right one switches to the composite and its rim pixels turn solid; the left stays pale. Readouts 'alpha 0.75' and 'alpha 1.0'.
B38.motion_claim: Focus lands on the three composite lines and the pale rim on the right turns solid while the left stays pale.
B38.runner_up: manim: a row of rim cells with alpha values
B38.why: The same rim before and after the one change, with the untouched twin beside it: the cure acting on the real pixels.

B40.capture_spec: C40-modulate: scene spec evidence/planning-checks/scenes/C40-modulate.json, 13.3 s clip (stretched to the measured audio), 30 fps, 1280x720 canvas rendered at 3840x2160, Forward+, nearest filter. Two sprites with the node's modulate faded to alpha 0.5: the left shader assigns COLOR from the texture and ignores the fade, the right passes the vertex COLOR on as a varying and fades with its line. Verified: with modulate alpha 0.5: no shader draws alpha 0.50; a shader assigning COLOR from the texture draws 1.00 (sprite) and 1.00 (line); the varying version draws 0.50 and 0.50 (verify_m M1)
B40.visual_intent: Code card at left: the 13-line modulate-safe shader (the varying tint, the one-line vertex function, and the final multiply by tint marked). At right two real sprites whose node modulate fades to half: the left one (its shader assigns color from the texture) stays fully solid with its line, the right one (vertex color kept) fades, line included. Readouts 'fade ignored' and 'fade works'.
B40.motion_claim: Both sprites are asked to fade; the left one does not, the right one does.

show.event: varying and multiply lines; right fades; readout 'fade works'
